# Diabetes Overview

Diabetes is a chronic metabolic condition where the body cannot properly regulate blood sugar (glucose) levels.

## Main Types

### Type 1 Diabetes
- Autoimmune condition where the body attacks insulin-producing cells
- Usually develops in childhood or young adulthood
- Requires lifelong insulin therapy

### Type 2 Diabetes
- Body becomes resistant to insulin or doesn't produce enough
- Most common form (90-95% of cases)
- Often linked to lifestyle factors and genetics
- May be managed with diet, exercise, and/or medication

### Gestational Diabetes
- Develops during pregnancy
- Usually resolves after delivery
- Increases risk of Type 2 diabetes later

## Common Symptoms
- Increased thirst and urination
- Unexplained weight loss
- Fatigue
- Blurred vision
- Slow-healing wounds

## Potential Complications
- Heart disease and stroke
- Kidney damage
- Nerve damage (neuropathy)
- Eye problems (retinopathy)
- Foot problems

## Management
- Blood sugar monitoring
- Healthy diet
- Regular physical activity
- Medications or insulin as needed
- Regular medical checkups
